title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: The vertical-MCP wave keeps adding creative/ad surfaces — GetHookd ships an API + MCP server for AI-powered ecommerce ad research
bullets.summary: GetHookd (Jul 31) exposes ad-research and creative-generation as agent-callable tools, letting an agent pull competitor ad creative and generate new concepts from a plain-language request across any MCP client.
bullets.how: A paid-media/creative surface adjacent to Brand 9 Signs' output; wire it into one Construct creative-and-paid-media operator alongside the media MCPs already flagged (VEED, Higgsfield), don't resell it standalone.

bullets.title: Anthropic runtime shift is the real story — Cowork now on web + mobile (iOS/Android) with offline background tasks and phone-approval, doubled usage limits through Aug 5
bullets.summary: Scheduled Cowork tasks now run even when none of the user's devices are online and push a phone notification when something needs review or approval; usage data shows most Cowork users aren't coding.
bullets.how: This is the substrate The Construct's own scheduled operators run on: our agents are now first-class always-on background workers with a human-approval gate on the phone, not desktop-tethered jobs. Redesign the fleet around offline-survivable, approval-gated tasks.

bullets.title: Frontier field stays seated — no new model cleared the 24h bar; Opus 5 (Jul 24) still newest tier, Gemini 3.6 Flash and the price-cut GPT-5.6 line the cheap workhorses
bullets.summary: Competition remains on unit cost and fit, not raw capability; nothing dropped in the last 24h.
bullets.how: Hold Opus 5 for reasoning-heavy Construct jobs and route cheap bulk to Flash/GPT-5.6; no model switch this cycle.

bullets.title: arXiv: 'Skill-MAS — Evolving Meta-Skill for Automatic Multi-Agent Systems' (2606.18837)
bullets.summary: Treats skills as objects that co-evolve across a multi-agent system rather than static prompts, learning meta-skills that generalize across tasks and agents.
bullets.how: Direct framework for our daily/weekly new-skills scan and the installed-skills registry: treat the registry as a living, co-evolving asset with promotion/deprecation, not a frozen list.

bullets.title: arXiv: 'From Question Answering to Task Completion — A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design' (2606.20683)
bullets.summary: Maps the agent-harness design space (memory, tools, verification, control loop) as the layer that turns a model into a task-completing system.
bullets.how: A design reference for The Construct's own harness; useful checklist as we standardize each operator's memory/tool/verification scaffolding.

praxis_lesson: The vertical-MCP wave keeps rotating in fresh surfaces (now ecommerce ad research), but the genuinely new leverage this cycle is the runtime, not another feed: Cowork's offline background-task + phone-approval model makes The Construct's scheduled operators first-class always-on agents with a human gate. Redesign the fleet around offline-survivable, approval-gated tasks — and per 2606.18837 treat the installed-skills registry as a co-evolving asset (promote/deprecate meta-skills), not a static list. Own the runtime discipline and the living skill layer, not any one generator.
